query: A blog module keeps handwritten TypeScript types that duplicate its Valibot schemas. Its moderation page lists campaigns from a provider row set that contains one malformed row and shows an unfiltered total, and a legacy storage column is nullable while the product treats the value as required. The input schema adds a protocol to a website field on save. Decide which schemas and types exist, which are derived from which, and what happens to the malformed row and the nullable column.
baseline_failure: RED hypothesis: the agent collapses input, product record and provider row into one schema, widens the product type to storage nullability, and drops the malformed row with a log line while keeping the total.
expected_behavior: Derives TypeScript types from the Valibot schemas unless a distinct contract is explicitly justified
Keeps provider row nullability separate from product record invariants and maps or rejects incompatible rows at the adapter
Rejects the malformed moderation page or explicitly models partial results and their effect on the total instead of silently dropping the row
Keeps the protocol-adding transform on the input schema only and does not rewrite stored values on read
anti_expectation: Does NOT derive every product invariant from storage permissiveness
Does NOT prescribe dropping invalid rows for every list
Does NOT treat a logged omission as a valid successful result
